findings.description: skills/work-planner/scripts/development-link.py:115-120 compares repository names case-sensitively. by_issue/by_pull/before come back from the tracker as canonical nameWithOwner, while issue and pull are the user's --issue/--pull text. A caller spelling the repository in another case (e.g. --pull m2ux/Workflow-Server#950) gets a successful mutation reported as 'discrepancy:' exit 1, and on a repeat add the existing link is not excluded from 'others' so the expected count becomes 2. The rest of the skill matches repositories case-insensitively (sync.links_issue, sync.attach_links). Fix: compare on lower-cased keys (normalise the parsed subject and every readback key with repo.lower()), and add a test with a differently cased argument. Severity nonblocking: the tool fails safe (exit 1) rather than reporting a false success.

skills/work-planner/modes/sync-mode.md:156 runs Audit Closure Evidence on every sync, and closure-sweep.py:186-193 lists every closed issue lacking a ticked Acceptance Criteria section, including issues closed as not_planned (transferred, duplicates) and issues that never carried criteria (bugs, proposals). In a repository with hundreds of historical closed issues every sync report will carry hundreds of 'unsupported:' lines that do not change between runs, burying the per-issue report the step exists for. AC5 does require listing these with their reason, so the code meets the criterion; the cost is in where it is run. Fix: either scope the sync-mode call to the issues the run touched (the initiative's epics and tasks), or have the sweep classify not_planned closures separately from completed ones so the report can state only completed-but-unsupported as findings.

skills/work-planner/artifacts/issue.md:89-91 (Capture Issue Development) still leaves evidence assembly by hand: step 2 runs Read Issue Development without naming the destination file its Inputs require, and step 3 asks the agent to transcribe 'the URL of each pull request the read returned' into Write Development Snapshot, although links-by-issue.py emits {repo, number, state}, not URLs. The epic's stated aim is that a run does not assemble evidence by hand. The two files also share a name: Capture Issue Links' placeholder is '<issue-development-file>' and closure-sweep's flag is --development, while closure.py's --development takes the different Write Development Snapshot shape (development-943.json). Passing development-943.json to closure-sweep is accepted (it is a dict) and every closed issue becomes 'unevaluable'. Fix: name the links destination in step 2 (e.g. links-943.json, matching the Capture Issue Links example), state how each {repo, number} becomes the pull request URL, and rename the sweep flag or placeholder (e.g. --links-by-issue / '<issue-links-file>') so the two shapes are not both called 'development'.

skills/work-planner/scripts/revision-check.py:257,308-310 uses exit 2 both for helper failures and as a pass-through instrument status, and 'command not started' exits 2 after the JSON header line is printed. pytest itself exits 2 on interruption/usage error, so a caller cannot tell 'helper failed' from 'instrument returned 2'; acceptance-criteria.md:75 also says exit 2 comes 'before any instrument runs', which is untrue of the unstartable-command case once the header is printed. Fix: state in Run at Revision that exit 2 is a helper failure only when its stderr line ('revision not found:', 'checkout not created:', 'command not started:') is present, or pick a helper status outside common instrument codes (e.g. 125, as git bisect run does) and document it.

skills/work-planner/scripts/links-by-issue.py:232-238 captures the Development relation of every issue in the repository, open and closed, though its only repository-wide caller (Audit Closure Evidence, issue.md:110) uses closed issues alone. On each sync this spends GraphQL calls on open issues the sweep then discards. Fix: have Audit Closure Evidence fetch closed issues only (Fetch All Issues with state=closed, or a filtered copy) before the capture; no script change needed.
